ram-bap-quang-ngai.name: Quang Ngai Corn Spring Rolls
ram-bap-quang-ngai.serving_basis: About 16 small corn rolls, served as a shared side or starter for four.
ram-bap-quang-ngai.description: Quang Ngai ram bap wraps young sticky corn with pork, shrimp, taro, shallot and chives in thin rice paper, then fries the rolls until golden. Bếp Việt edits a family-size recipe from local descriptions, keeping the sweet, tender corn filling and small crisp rolls.
ram-bap-quang-ngai.finished_dish: Small crisp golden rolls with a sweet, tender corn filling, fragrant chives and pepper, and a lightly savory taste from pork and shrimp.
ram-bap-quang-ngai.serving: Serve hot with fresh greens, cucumber and sweet-sour garlic fish sauce. The rolls can also be wrapped in rice paper with greens.
tips: Choose young sticky corn with milky kernels; very young corn is watery, while mature corn can be tough.
Cook the filling until dry and let it cool before rolling so the wrappers do not tear or splatter in the oil.
Make small rolls and fry in batches; wait until the underside sets before turning.
ram-bap-quang-ngai.image_alt: A plate of golden Quang Ngai corn rolls, including one cut open to show its young sticky-corn filling; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
ram-bap-quang-ngai.time_note: About 1 hour, including 10 minutes to cool the filling before rolling.

ingredients.name: Young sticky corn kernels
ingredients.notes: Shave the kernels from the cob and lightly pound; do not puree.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: Pork shoulder with a little fat keeps the filling moist.

ingredients.name: Peeled fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Finely chop; omit for a vegetarian version.

ingredients.name: Taro
ingredients.notes: Peel, grate and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Rice-paper wrappers for rolls
ingredients.notes: Choose thin, pliable small wrappers; cut larger sheets in half if needed.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Garlic chives
ingredients.notes: Rinse and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly; saltiness varies by brand.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional, to soften the savory flavor.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Freshly ground if available.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season to taste.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Enough to submerge the rolls in a small pan; not all of it will be absorbed.

ingredients.name: Fresh greens
ingredients.notes: Rinse and drain thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice.

preparation_steps: Rinse the corn, shave the kernels from the cob and lightly pound them in a mortar until some kernels split and the mixture starts to hold together. Chop the shrimp, grate and chop the taro, mince the shallot and chop the chives.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pan and cook the shallot for about 30 seconds. Add the pork and shrimp and stir until just cooked. Add the taro, corn, fish sauce, sugar, salt and pepper; cook for 4–5 minutes until the filling is cohesive and no liquid pools in the pan. Stir in the chives, spread the filling on a plate and cool for 10 minutes.
cooking_steps: Divide the filling into 16 portions. Place each on a rice-paper wrapper and roll into a small 7–8 cm cylinder, folding in both ends. If the wrapper is dry, dab a little water on the edge to seal.

Heat the oil over medium heat to about 165–170°C. Fry the rolls in batches, leaving them undisturbed until the wrappers set; turn and fry for 4–6 minutes per batch until evenly golden. Drain in a rack.
Serve hot with fresh greens, cucumber and a bowl of sweet-sour garlic chili fish sauce.

banh-bo-quang-ngai.name: Quang Ngai Bánh Bó Pressed Cake
aliases: Quang Ngai Lunar New Year bánh bó
banh-bo-quang-ngai.serving_basis: One small pressed cake, cut into about 12 slices to share among four.
banh-bo-quang-ngai.description: Bánh bó is a pressed glutinous-rice cake associated with Quang Ngai’s Lunar New Year spread. Toasted glutinous rice flour is bound with sugar syrup and mixed with candied coconut, pineapple, carrot, winter melon, tomato and ginger. Bếp Việt edits a small-batch home version using ready-made glutinous rice flour toasted at home.
banh-bo-quang-ngai.finished_dish: Chewy fragrant white rice cake flecked with colorful candied fruit, gently sweet with rich coconut, pineapple and a faint warmth of ginger.
banh-bo-quang-ngai.serving: Let the cake cool and firm up, then slice thinly with a lightly oiled knife. Serve with hot tea; wrap leftovers and eat the same day.
tips: Cut the fruit and vegetables into fine strips, simmer the preserve until nearly dry, and let it cool completely so the flour does not become wet.
Toast the glutinous rice flour over low heat, stirring constantly so it dries and smells fragrant without browning.
Pour the hot syrup into the flour gradually; stop when the dough just holds together because flours absorb different amounts of liquid.
dish_type: Quang Ngai Lunar New Year cake
search_terms: Quang Ngai Lunar New Year cake
banh-bo-quang-ngai.image_alt: A short log of Quang Ngai bánh bó sliced to show colorful coconut, pineapple, carrot and winter-melon preserves in white glutinous rice dough; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
banh-bo-quang-ngai.time_note: About 1 hour 30 minutes, including time for the preserves to cool and the cake to firm before slicing.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice flour
ingredients.notes: Use food-grade glutinous rice flour and dry-toast it in a pan before kneading.

ingredients.name: Grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Use fresh coconut flesh cut into fine strips.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove the eyes and cut into fine strips.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into fine strips.

ingredients.name: Winter melon
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove the seeds and cut into strips.

ingredients.name: Firm ripe tomato
ingredients.notes: Remove the watery seeds and cut into strips.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into very fine strips.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Divide between the fruit preserves and the syrup.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the sugar syrup that binds the flour.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: A small pinch balances the sweetness.

preparation_steps: Cut the coconut, pineapple, carrot, winter melon, tomato and ginger into fine strips. Mix them in a pan with 90 g sugar and leave for 10 minutes to release their juices.
Toast the glutinous rice flour in a dry pan over low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring constantly until fragrant and free-flowing but not browned. Transfer to a large bowl.
cooking_steps: Set the fruit pan over medium-low heat and simmer, stirring gently, for 12–15 minutes until the strips look translucent and little syrup remains. Spread the preserves on a plate and cool completely for about 20 minutes.

Bring the remaining sugar and 100 ml water to a gentle boil for 4–5 minutes until the sugar dissolves and forms a light syrup. Turn off the heat and gradually pour the hot syrup into the flour, stirring until a soft cohesive dough forms; you may not need all the syrup.
Fold in the cooled preserves and knead quickly to distribute them. Flatten to 1.5–2 cm thick and roll tightly into a log using parchment or food wrap; rest for 20 minutes until firm, then slice.

banh-no-quang-ngai.name: Quang Ngai Bánh Nổ Puffed Rice Cake
aliases: Quang Ngai Lunar New Year puffed rice cake
banh-no-quang-ngai.serving_basis: One small pan of pressed cake cut into about 16 pieces, or four snack portions.
banh-no-quang-ngai.description: Quang Ngai bánh nổ is made from puffed sticky rice, sugar and ginger. The puffed rice is quickly mixed with ginger syrup, packed firmly into a mold, dried and cut into pieces. Bếp Việt adapts the method for a home kitchen by using ready-puffed food-grade sticky rice while keeping the binding, pressing and ginger aroma of the traditional cake.
banh-no-quang-ngai.finished_dish: Ivory square pieces that are light and crisp, with puffed rice grains held together by a thin layer of ginger-scented sugar.
banh-no-quang-ngai.serving: Let the cake cool completely before cutting so the edges stay neat. Serve with hot tea and store in an airtight container once cool.
tips: Choose dry, crisp puffed sticky rice without a stale smell; soft grains make chewy cake.
Cook the syrup until just thick enough to coat a spoon; dark caramel makes the cake hard and bitter.
Press the mixture firmly while it is hot; work quickly because cooled syrup will no longer bind well.
dish_type: Quang Ngai Lunar New Year cake
search_terms: Quang Ngai Lunar New Year cake
banh-no-quang-ngai.image_alt: Ivory square pieces of Quang Ngai bánh nổ pressed from puffed sticky-rice grains bound with ginger syrup; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
banh-no-quang-ngai.time_note: About 1 hour 5 minutes, including 30 minutes for the cake to set and cool before cutting.

ingredients.name: Ready-puffed sticky rice
ingredients.notes: Use puffed or popped sticky rice sold as food from a trusted supplier.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Cook into syrup to bind the puffed rice.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into fine strips.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the syrup.

preparation_steps: Prepare a roughly 16 × 16 cm square mold and line it with parchment. Check the puffed rice and remove burnt or hard grains; gently separate any clumps.
Peel the ginger and cut it into fine strips. Measure the puffed rice and place a heatproof spatula beside the stove so you can mix as soon as the syrup is ready.
cooking_steps: Put the sugar, water and ginger in a small pan. Heat over medium, stirring until the sugar dissolves; simmer gently for 5–7 minutes until the syrup thickens slightly and falls from a spoon in a fine thread.
Remove the pan from the heat and immediately add the puffed rice. Fold quickly and gently until the syrup coats the grains.

Transfer the mixture to the lined mold, cover with another sheet of parchment and press very firmly with the flat bottom of a cup. Leave in a cool, dry place for 30 minutes until fully set, then cut into 16 pieces.

xu-xoa-quang-ngai.name: Quang Ngai Xu Xoa Seaweed Jelly
xu-xoa-quang-ngai.serving_basis: Four bowls of chilled xu xoa with ginger sugar syrup, served as dessert or a cooling snack.
xu-xoa-quang-ngai.description: Quang Ngai xu xoa is a clear jelly made from seaweed gathered along the local rocky shore. Dried seaweed is soaked and rinsed repeatedly, simmered with water and a little lemon until soft, then strained and left to set. Bếp Việt edits a small batch and serves it with fresh ginger sugar syrup, as locals do.
xu-xoa-quang-ngai.finished_dish: Clear, softly crisp seaweed jelly served chilled with pale amber ginger syrup.
xu-xoa-quang-ngai.serving: Cut the xu xoa into small cubes and divide among bowls. Pour over cooled ginger syrup and add ice just before serving if desired.
tips: Use only dried xu xoa seaweed sold as food by a trusted supplier; do not gather seaweed from a beach yourself.
Rinse and remove sand and shell fragments several times; a fine strainer helps the jelly stay clear and smooth.
Use lemon juice sparingly; simmer until the seaweed breaks down and strain while hot.
xu-xoa-quang-ngai.image_alt: A clear glass bowl of translucent Quang Ngai xu xoa seaweed jelly cubes with pale amber ginger syrup; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
xu-xoa-quang-ngai.time_note: About 6 hours, mostly 4 hours to soak the seaweed and 1 hour to chill the jelly until set.

ingredients.name: Dried edible seaweed for xu xoa
ingredients.notes: Use prepared xu xoa seaweed sold as food; pick out sand and shells.

ingredients.name: Water for the jelly
ingredients.notes: Adjust slightly depending on the seaweed and desired firmness.

ingredients.name: Lemon juice
ingredients.notes: Strain out the seeds; helps the seaweed soften as it cooks.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: For the ginger syrup; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Water for the syrup
ingredients.notes: For making the ginger syrup.

ingredients.name: Ice cubes
ingredients.notes: Optional; add when serving.

preparation_steps: Spread out the dried seaweed and remove sand, shell fragments and debris. Rinse several times until the water is less cloudy, then soak in cool water for 4 hours.
Drain the seaweed, rinse twice more and set aside. Peel and slice the ginger; squeeze and strain the lemon juice.
cooking_steps: Put the soaked seaweed in a pot with 1.8 liters water and the lemon juice. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer, stirring, for 30–35 minutes until the seaweed breaks down.
While hot, strain the mixture through a fine sieve or clean cloth into a shallow tray. Let it cool naturally, then refrigerate for about 1 hour until firmly set.
Meanwhile, simmer 250 ml water with the sugar and ginger for 5–7 minutes. Turn off the heat and cool the syrup; taste and add a little water if a lighter flavor is preferred.
Cut the jelly into cubes, divide among four bowls, pour over the ginger syrup and add ice if using.

mit-hong-tam-ky.name: Tam Ky Steamed Stuffed Jackfruit
mit-hong-tam-ky.serving_basis: About 12–16 small stuffed jackfruit bulbs, divided into four snack portions.
mit-hong-tam-ky.description: Mít hông Tam Kỳ is a home-style treat associated with Tam Ky, now in the southern part of Da Nang. Ripe jackfruit bulbs are seeded; the seeds are boiled, mashed and lightly seasoned, then stuffed back into the bulbs and steamed. Bếp Việt standardizes a small batch and keeps the local finish of grated coconut and roasted peanuts.
mit-hong-tam-ky.finished_dish: Soft, sweet ripe jackfruit bulbs filled with a smooth, nutty jackfruit-seed mash, finished with fragrant coconut and roasted peanuts.
mit-hong-tam-ky.serving: Sprinkle with grated coconut and peanuts just before eating. Serve warm or at room temperature as a snack.
tips: Choose fragrant ripe jackfruit bulbs that still hold their shape; overripe fruit is difficult to slit and fill.
Boil the seeds until a skewer passes through easily, then remove the papery skins before mashing for a smooth filling.
Steam only until hot and tender; too much steaming can make the bulbs collapse or split.
mit-hong-tam-ky.image_alt: Tam Ky mít hông on a plate: ripe jackfruit bulbs stuffed with mashed jackfruit seeds and topped with grated coconut and roasted peanuts; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
mit-hong-tam-ky.time_note: About 50 minutes, including boiling the jackfruit seeds and steaming the stuffed bulbs.

ingredients.name: Seeded ripe jackfruit bulbs
ingredients.notes: Keep the bulbs intact so they can be slit and filled.

ingredients.name: Jackfruit seeds, hard shells removed
ingredients.notes: Rinse; boil until tender, then remove any papery skin that remains.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Mix into the mashed seeds; adjust to the sweetness of the fruit.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: A small pinch seasons the filling.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add only if the mashed filling is too dry.

ingredients.name: Grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the dish before serving.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush lightly and sprinkle over the dish.

preparation_steps: Separate the ripe jackfruit bulbs, remove any seeds that remain and keep the bulbs intact. Make a lengthwise slit in each bulb to form a small pocket.
Rinse the jackfruit seeds and remove their hard shells if they are still on. Prepare a steamer and lightly crush the roasted peanuts.
cooking_steps: Put the jackfruit seeds in a pot of water and simmer for 15–20 minutes until a skewer passes through easily. Drain, remove any papery brown skin and mash with the sugar and salt until smooth and nutty; add a little water if needed.
Fill each jackfruit bulb with the seed mash without overpacking it. Arrange in a steamer over boiling water, cover and steam for 10–12 minutes until the fruit is warm and tender.
Transfer the stuffed jackfruit to a plate and sprinkle with grated coconut and crushed roasted peanuts. Serve warm or let cool slightly before eating.
